name: Agent Gateway
description: Deploys the official agentgateway binary as an MCP federation proxy. One public HTTP listener on port 8080 serves the UI (HTTP basic auth) and a Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint (Bearer API key or the same basic-auth credentials) that multiplexes tools from backends such as ha-mcp LXCs.

notes.text: Public listener is 0.0.0.0:8080 (var_public_port, default 8080). UI: http://<container-ip>:8080/ui with HTTP basic auth (default user admin, random password). MCP Streamable HTTP: http://<container-ip>:8080/mcp/http (also /mcp and /sse). Copy /opt/agentgateway/mcp_client.json into your MCP client's config (Bearer API key). MCP also accepts the same basic-auth credentials. Tools are always prefixed with the target name (prefixMode: always). One dead backend does not fail the whole session (failureMode: failOpen).

UI and MCP share one 1.4 gateways listener. Two strict auth policies would both have to succeed (AND), so MCP uses optional apiKey + optional basicAuth plus a CEL allow rule so Bearer token OR basic auth works. UI uses basicAuth mode strict only. Basic auth is not TLS; keep this on a LAN or behind a TLS reverse proxy.

Prometheus metrics (15020) and readiness (15021) bind to 127.0.0.1. The process also keeps an unauthenticated loopback admin socket on 127.0.0.1:15000 as break-glass (not advertised; do not publish 15000/15020/15021). Optional: var_admin_port / var_admin_bind — leave bind at 127.0.0.1.

Install does not prompt for backends. After install, add Streamable HTTP servers in the UI (MCP → Servers) or in /opt/agentgateway/config.yaml under mcp.targets. Example: name home, URL from `pct exec <CTID> -- cat /opt/ha-mcp/mcp_endpoint.txt`. Target names: letters, digits, hyphens only (no underscores). mcp.targets must be present even if empty (`targets: []`).

Unattended: `bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oraad/proxmox-scripts/main/ct/agentgateway.sh)"`. Optional backends: `var_mcp_targets='home=http://192.168.1.21:8086/mcp-secret'`. Optional: `var_public_port=8080` (alias `var_mcp_port`), `var_ui_user=admin`, `var_ui_password=...`, `var_api_key=...`. Loopback admin: `var_admin_port=15000 var_admin_bind=127.0.0.1`.

Config: /opt/agentgateway/config.yaml (mode 600, user agentgateway). Basic-auth hashes live in /opt/agentgateway/htpasswd. Saving in the UI overwrites config.yaml and strips comments. `config.*` binds and session.key are only applied at process start — restart after changing them. Most other YAML edits hot-reload.
Keep one ha-mcp LXC per Home Assistant. This gateway federates their HTTP endpoints and never sees HA tokens. Do not also register the same ha-mcp URLs directly in the MCP client.

Update an existing container: run `update` inside the LXC, or `pct exec <CTID> -- update` from the Proxmox host. Updates replace the binary and leave config.yaml / .env in place. Dry-run via PVE LXC Apps Updater works (check_for_gh_release).

Retrieve the MCP URL with `pct exec <CTID> -- cat /opt/agentgateway/mcp_endpoint.txt`. UI URL: `pct exec <CTID> -- cat /opt/agentgateway/ui_url.txt`. MCP client snippet: `pct exec <CTID> -- cat /opt/agentgateway/mcp_client.json`. Secrets (API key, UI password): `pct exec <CTID> -- grep -E 'AGENTGATEWAY_API_KEY|UI_USER|UI_PASSWORD' /opt/agentgateway/.env`.

Service status — Debian: `systemctl status agentgateway` and `journalctl -u agentgateway -n 50`. Alpine: `rc-service agentgateway status` and `tail -50 /var/log/agentgateway.log`. Official docs: https://agentgateway.dev/docs/standalone/latest/mcp/connect/virtual/

Alpine template: run `pveam update`, then `pveam available --section system | grep alpine-3.23`. Download if missing: `pveam download local alpine-3.23-default_20260116_amd64.tar.xz` (use the exact name from `pveam available` on your arch). Fallback: `var_version=3.22` if 3.23 is not listed on an older Proxmox host. The upstream binary is musl (amd64/arm64).
Debian 13 and Alpine installs enable nesting and keyctl by default (Debian: systemd compatibility; Alpine: Docker and tunnel agents).
